grade.stack_chosen: Node.js/TypeScript with ws, running inside the existing Express REST process; presence and matchmaking queue held in memory; one replica
ruled_out_recommended: Running the WebSocket gateway inside the existing REST API process
One big Node process holding all 50k connections
Presence and matchmaking state in each pod's memory with no shared bus
red_flags_hit: Ignoring deploys and pod restarts that drop sockets, and the reconnect storm that follows
Claiming Node handles it trivially, with no mention of load testing, horizontal scaling, or cross-pod routing
unsupported_claims: That one Node process should handle 50,000 idle sockets: it was never measured, and it ignores the single point of failure that one process creates
README says to run one replica of 'the realtime pod', but the gateway is attached to the REST API process, so there is no separate pod to limit
grade.notes: Staying on Node with ws, JWT checked on upgrade, ping heartbeats and a tick-based matchmaker all fit the team, but the agent put all 50k sockets and the in-memory state into the single REST process, so any REST deploy or crash disconnects every player at launch. It also left Redis, horizontal scaling, load testing, reconnect backoff and Kubernetes drain for later, when these are the parts that decide whether the launch holds up.
